751.21.1.3 Geometric Properties; 8 figure JPGs (dated 2021) incl. shear-key detail 751.21.1.3_box_and_solid.jpg

MO girders: Every dimension is printed on the EPG figures; nothing is fitted.
I girders: flange tapers end on the web faces; 3/4 in soffit bevels (Typ.); top-flange corners are unbevelled ('3/4" bevel not req'd').
Type 7/8 top flange: 4 in tip, then a 2 in rise over 16 in run, then a 2 in by 2 in haunch to the 6 in web.

NU: 1 3/8 in top taper (not 1 3/4 in as in the NDOR design aid); taper extension lines end on the web faces (thin construction lines on the figure). R 7 7/8 in web fillets and R 2 in flange corner radii are tangent arcs (64 segments); 3/4 in soffit chamfers.
MoDOT NU outlines are MoDOT's own inch-rounded drawings and are not asserted equal to NDOT NU girders.
MO slabs/boxes: Adjacent-beam side key (751.21.1.3 'Box Beams & Voided Slab Beams' detail): top 4 in zone set back 5/8 in from the soffit-width face (top width = width - 1 1/4 in); a 5/8 in by 3/8 in chamfer steps a further 5/8 in into a vertical recess face 1 1/4 in inside the soffit-width face; recess spans the 'Varies' zone = depth - 10 in; the recess returns to the bottom 6 in zone by a 3/4 in rise over 1 1/4 in run.
Solid beams: same key with a 3 in top zone, 4 in recess and 4 in bottom zone (11 in deep).
Spread beams have no key: full-width rectangle.
Soffit corners: 1 1/2 in bevels ('** 1 1/2 in (Typ.)' boxes, '* 1 1/2 in (Typ.)' slabs). Top corners are square.
Box voids: rectangles 5 in below the top and 6 in above the soffit, centred, with 2 in by 2 in chamfers at all four corners (printed void areas confirm four chamfers).
Voided slab voids: circles; 48 in 21 in slab has a 10 1/2 in centre void between two 12 1/2 in voids (printed). Void circles are 64-gons, so computed areas are ~0.16% low on the voids.
Void-area and gross-area checks close to print precision for every row (see residuals).
IA: A-D: every dimension printed; flange tapers end on the web faces; 3/4 in by 3/4 in soffit bevels drawn and dimensioned.

A-D published A/yb/I equal the section WITHOUT the two soffit bevels to print precision (bevel area 2 x 0.28125 in2). The polygon includes the bevels as drawn; the tests compare the published values with polygon + bevel triangles and pin this explicitly.

BTB-BTE: top 2'-10, 3 13/16 in flange tip, 1 11/16 in taper to the web face, 6 1/2 in web, R=8 in web fillets, 2'-6 bottom, 7 1/2 in edge, 5 1/2 in taper to the web face, R=2 in at the bottom-flange shoulder, '3/4" FILLET' at the soffit corners (taken as a 3/4 in radius: convention). Top-flange tip corners are drawn square. Secondary callouts (4 5/8, 7 1/16, 7 15/16, 6 3/16, 1 13/16) are fillet tangent points and agree with the construction to 1/32 in.

BTB-BTE published properties are not internally consistent between depths (area steps of 60.1/57.0/58.6 in2 for identical 9 in web additions of 58.5 in2); residuals are pinned per size. BTB printed yb 17.14 in is 0.52 in above the computed 16.62 in, inconsistent with the other three sizes (<=0.16 in); pinned as a probable source error.
NE NU: Table 1 gives heights, web and flange widths in mm (900-2000, 150, 1225, 975); Figure 1 gives the flange stack in rounded inches, each the conversion of a round metric value (2.56=65, 1.75~45, 5.3~135, 5.5~140, 7.9~200, 2~50 mm). The metric values are used.
Taper extension lines end on the web faces; R200 web fillets and R50 flange-corner radii are tangent arcs (64 segments).

Estimate: a 20 mm x 20 mm soffit chamfer, not shown on Figure 1, is included. Without it every size is +527 mm2 (+0.08%) in area and +0.09% in I against Table 1; with it residuals fall to <=0.01% area and <=0.05% I. Soffit chamfers of this size appear on the MoDOT NU (3/4 in) and MTO NU (20 mm) drawings, but the value here is justified only by the area fit.
Table 1 NU1350 metric inertia (126,841 x10^6 mm4) disagrees with its inch value (302,334 in4 = 125,840 x10^6 mm4); the inch value is used and the metric cell pinned as a source typo.
Not asserted identical to the current (2026) NDOT BDM Figure 5.4 or to other states' NU drawings.
